reader.requirement: At --std 85 every report file is placed in one of the three categories (non-reel/unit, sequential single-reel/unit, sequential multi-reel/unit), and each CLOSE format then has that category's Table 1 effect (GR3). WiseOwl COBOL puts every report file in (a) non-reel/unit, so CLOSE = C, CLOSE WITH LOCK = C,E, CLOSE WITH NO REWIND = C,H (closed, phrase ignored), CLOSE REEL/UNIT [FOR REMOVAL] = F non-reel (successful, file stays open, nothing else happens), with status 07 for the phrase forms (VII.1.3.5 1d).

reader.notes: The 1985 Report Writer table has three columns and the 2023 Table 14 four; the code keys on the 2023 table, but its non-unit column is cell for cell the same as 1985's non-reel column (C; C,E; C,H; F; F), and report files are only ever sequential, so the fourth column never applies. The categorization is the implementor's medium choice and is documented (A.1 item 24).

refuter.evidence: The 1985 CLOSE general rules open with a sentence the later editions dropped, which the reader's requirement and notes do not mention: 'Treatment of sequential mass storage files is logically equivalent to the treatment of a file on tape or analogous sequential media.' (cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.4.2.4, the text is in the clause; the 2002, 2014 and 2023 texts carry only the reel/unit-multiple-device sentence, grep of specs/ISO_COBOL_20xx.md). A report file the compiler writes to a host path is a sequential mass storage file (§1985 definitions 'Mass Storage File', 'Mass Storage'). Read literally, at --std 85 such a file belongs in GR2 category b (sequential single-reel/unit), not a (non-reel/unit), and then Table 1 gives CLOSE WITH NO REWIND = B,C and CLOSE REEL/UNIT [FOR REMOVAL] = F,G / D,F,G with status 00, while 07 (§1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.1d, 'the referenced file is on a non-reel/unit medium') would be owed only on a unit-record medium. The compiler answers 07 for all three (reader's p1close: REEL=07 UNITREM=07 NOREW=07; my r5 probe OPEN OUTPUT PRT WITH NO REWIND = 07). The placement doc the reader leans on, docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-24.md, derives category (a) from the 2023 text alone and calls it 'FORCED' by 2023's 07 definition; that argument does not carry to 1985, where 07 has a home (a printer or terminal) and the preamble sends mass storage to the tape columns, and docs/conformance/3/D-IO-STATUS-07-OPEN-CLOSE.md itself records that its determination 'has not yet been read against' the 1985 text (kb/Work PB5256). Against the literal reading: GR2a defines category a by the medium on which 'the concepts of rewind and reels/units have no meaning', which a host file meets in fact, and the 1985 NIST suite (tests/nist/programs/SQ123A.cob, X-14 'SEQUENTIAL NON-UNIT MASS STORAGE FILE') treats a sequential mass storage file as non-unit and expects 07 from CLOSE REEL. The verdict therefore rests on reading 'logically equivalent' as not fixing the GR2 category; the text does not settle it.
refuter.corrected: If the preamble governs the category: NON-CONFORMING (wrong-answer, cause c: the 1985 text covers more than the 2023-derived placement accounts for) - a disk-resident report file is category b at --std 85, so CLOSE WITH NO REWIND, CLOSE REEL/UNIT and CLOSE REEL/UNIT FOR REMOVAL should succeed with 00 (B,C; F,G; D,F,G), not 07; at 2023 the 07 is right. Needs a ruling (and a re-read of DOC-A.1-24 / D-IO-STATUS-07 against §1985:XIII.4.2.4 and VII.4.2.4, kb/Work PB5256).
